identity.name: POS X Beta Phase 1
identity.description: Active POS X development — a two-tier POS system (Lite and Growth) targeting first live customer deployment.

goals: Launch POS X to at least one live end-customer — this is goal zero; everything else serves it
Deliver the Lite tier (single-location, streamlined POS) as a complete, sellable product — not a demo
Deliver the Growth tier (multi-location, warehouse, advanced pricing, purchase orders, RBAC) for scaling businesses
Implement the feature gating framework (hidden vs disabled-with-tooltip vs fully available) cleanly across all 10 module areas from the feature matrix
Cover core ERP workflows: Register, Product Catalog, Pricing, Customer, Stock/Inventory, Purchase, Sales Controls, Finance, Document Control
Build for depth over time — the architecture must support adding V8-level richness module by module through the BPX product process, not ad-hoc feature creep
Maintain code quality and test coverage standards throughout rapid development

milestones.name: Lite tier feature-complete (all 10 module areas from feature matrix)
Growth tier feature-complete (multi-location, warehouse, advanced pricing, PO, RBAC)
Feature gating framework live (Lite vs Growth toggle working end-to-end)
Internal pilot (team using POS X for real transactions)
First external customer live on POS X

kpis.name: Feature matrix coverage (features implemented vs spec)

risks.description: Scope creep — features added outside BPX pipeline delay launch
risks.mitigation: Enforce BPX as single intake; zero tolerance for side-channel requests

risks.description: Lite vs Growth feature gating becomes inconsistent or breaks across modules
risks.mitigation: Centralised gating framework with automated tests; feature matrix as regression baseline

risks.description: First customer launch fails due to undiscovered edge cases in real transactions
risks.mitigation: Internal pilot with real transaction data before external launch; dedicated beta support channel

risks.description: Team split between V8 maintenance and POS X slows both
risks.mitigation: Clear resource allocation; V8 in maintenance mode with minimal dev investment

risks.description: V8 feature depth expectations not met — customers expect V8 maturity from day one
risks.mitigation: Explicit Lite/Growth positioning; manage expectations through BPX gap analysis

dependencies.description: PRDs and feature specs — PXB1 builds what BPX defines
POS X deployment infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines
Test case coverage for quality gates before launch
V8 as reference implementation — feature parity comparison baseline
Analytics and reporting capabilities for POS X

notes: This is the future of the company. Phase 1 ships a two-tier POS: Lite (single-location, streamlined) and Growth (multi-location, warehouse, advanced pricing, RBAC). The feature matrix (PXB-A-238) is the definitive spec for what's in each tier. Goal zero is one live customer — everything else is secondary. The product must gain depth over time to match V8's maturity, but through BPX's product process, not ad-hoc. YouTrack schema differs from V8 — work type is 'TaskType' here, not 'Type'. The old PXB project is dormant; PXB1 is the active one.
